name: Lomé Data Centre (LDC / SIN-1-LOME)
developer: Société d'Infrastructures Numériques (SIN) / State of Togo; management per DataCenterMap listing attributed to Africa Data Centres (2021 role)
notes: Togo's first carrier-neutral colocation data centre / carrier hotel, inaugurated 4 June 2021 by President Faure Gnassingbé; located in Lomé on a ~1-hectare plot (Quartier Atchante, Route de la Nouvelle Présidence). World Bank WARCIP additional financing ($30m + $11m, press release 2021-05-24) supported construction of the carrier-neutral colocation facility as a regional bandwidth hub. Tier III certified (Uptime Institute listing 'SIN-1-LOME Data Centre, Lomé'; Connecting Africa describes facility as Tier III-certified). DCD reported ~400 sqm private-sector + ~100 sqm government floorspace at opening; operator markets 1+ MW and 800+ m2 usable space — capacity_mw=1.0 is the operator marketing value per methodology (not an audited IT load). Evidence grade A for existence (official site + World Bank + Uptime Institute); B for technical details (DCD). PIA Adétikopé industrial park (Maritime) remains a watch zone with no datacenter tenant evidence — no facility record built.

name: SIN + ST Digital private cloud at Lomé Data Centre
notes: Service-level record, not a new physical datacenter: SIN and ST Digital signed a strategic partnership to launch private cloud services deployed at the existing Lomé Data Centre facility. ST Digital markets a redundant data centre (99.99% availability, multi-operator fibre access across West Africa) hosted at LDC. Per TG methodology this is separated from the LDC facility record.

name: Togo Internet Exchange Point (TGIX / TogoIX)
notes: Interconnection asset (IXP), not commercial DC capacity: TGIX operational in Lomé since 15 June 2017; ~9 peers / 18G total capacity per PeeringDB/ISOC Pulse (PeeringDB updated July 2026).

name: WACS landing station - Lomé/Afidegnigba
notes: Interconnection asset (submarine cable landing), not commercial DC capacity: West Africa Cable System (WACS) central landing inaugurated in Afidegnigba, Lomé per Togo Telecom. Confirms the methodology's WACS direct-landing record.

name: Equiano cable landing station - Lomé (CLS)
developer: CSquared Woezon (56% CSquared / 44% SIN) with Google
notes: Interconnection asset (submarine cable landing), not commercial DC capacity: Google's Equiano subsea cable landed in Lomé on 18 March 2022 (its first African landing); CSquared Woezon (with SIN) operates/maintains the cable landing station. Government/official announcement (Cina Lawson ministry oversaw landing; Wikipedia/cross-source) + operator pages.
